transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I can’t seem to keep my work in order anymore. At the laundry, I’ve got tickets, receipts, notes, customer jobs—all of it ends up piled together, and then I don’t know what to handle first. It’s getting hard to manage.
Is this difficulty with organization and managing tasks only happening at work, or are you experiencing it in other parts of your life as well?

It’s mostly what I’m noticing at work. I mean, that’s where it’s really causing trouble—tickets, receipts, notes from the workshop, customer jobs, they all end up in one pile and then I can’t figure out what to do first. I’m not saying it never happens elsewhere, but work is the main place I’m seeing it.
How much distress or anxiety are you experiencing because of this disorganization at work?

I’m not really sure how to rate it. It bothers me because it makes the day harder and I feel pressured when things pile up, but I don’t know if I’d call it anxiety exactly. It’s just frustrating and stressful when I can’t get it sorted.
Are you noticing any difficulties in your personal relationships due to your current situation?

Yes, some. At the shop it’s caused tense moments with the staff and with customers when orders are late or the billing gets mixed up. That’s been hard.

And outside work, at church, I’ve stepped back from helping lead some planning because people were getting frustrated with me. I don’t like that, but it felt like I was causing more problems than helping.
Do you find yourself easily distracted by things around you while trying to focus on a task?

Yes, I do. Like when I’m going over the day’s dry-cleaning orders, I can start out okay, but after a few minutes my mind has wandered to the labels, or choir plans, or something I need to do at home. Then I kind of snap back and realize I missed half of what I was supposed to be checking.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Yes, I think so. If I’m in a church committee meeting or one of those fabric-care trainings, I have a hard time just staying seated. I’ll keep finding reasons to get up—get water, grab papers, check on something—even when everyone else is sitting still.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Yes, I do. I’ll jump in with an answer before someone’s even finished asking me—like my daughter, or a customer at work, or a trainer. Then sometimes I realize I answered the wrong question because I didn’t wait to hear the whole thing. It’s embarrassing.
Do you often feel like you're constantly on the go, even when you're not necessarily needing to be?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I do keep busy a lot, but I haven’t really thought of it as feeling “constantly on the go.” I guess I’d need to think about what you mean by that.
Do you have trouble following through on instructions or finishing tasks in your personal life, like at home or with hobbies?

Yes. If somebody gives me a few things to do, I’ll usually start with the first one, and then I get pulled off into something else before I finish the rest. Like if I’m supposed to call the supplier, tag a silk blouse, and enter a receipt, I might make the call and then the other two just don’t get done unless someone reminds me.
Do you have intense mood swings, where you quickly become very angry, excited, or upset?
I’m not sure I’d call it intense mood swings. I can get irritated or upset sometimes, like anyone, but I haven’t really noticed it changing suddenly or getting extreme.
Do you often find yourself engaging in excessive running, climbing, or other physical activities in your free time?
No, not really. I don’t usually run around or climb on things or anything like that in my free time. I might keep busy, but not in that kind of way.
Do you have difficulty sustaining focus on tasks that require mental effort over a long period of time?

Yes, I do. I can start going through the day’s dry-cleaning orders just fine, but after a few minutes my mind is somewhere else — like thinking about labels, or choir plans, or something I need to do at home. Then I’ll look back and realize I missed half of what I was supposed to be checking.
Have you always had difficulty with organization and focus, or is this something that has developed more recently?

I think it’s been there a long time. Even back in grade school, my teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but scattered. I’d talk out of turn, lose papers, and need reminders to actually finish my work. So no, it’s not really new.
How old were you when you first started noticing these difficulties with organization and focus?

I’d say I first noticed it in grade school, or at least that’s when adults were pointing it out. My teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but scattered — I’d talk out of turn, lose papers, and need reminders to finish my work.
Have you experienced difficulties with organization, focus, or impulsivity consistently throughout your life, from childhood to the present?

Yes, it’s been pretty consistent. Like I said, even in grade school my teachers would tell my mother I was bright but scattered. I was always talking out of turn, losing papers, and needing reminders to finish my work. It feels like that pattern has just kind of followed me along.
Have your symptoms of disorganization, impulsivity, and difficulty with focus significantly interfered with your ability to function effectively in your daily life or maintain relationships?

Yes, it has. At work in the laundry shop, it’s caused real problems — late orders, mixing up or confusing the billing, and then things get tense with coworkers or customers. And at church, I’ve backed away from helping lead some planning because people were getting frustrated with me. It’s embarrassing, but it has affected things.
Have you experienced difficulties with organization, focus, or impulsivity in social situations outside of work and church?

Yes. Even outside of work and church, I’ll sometimes jump into other people’s conversations before they’re really asking me. Or if someone’s doing something, I might reach over and try to fix it myself before they ask. I know it can come off like I’m butting in, and I don’t mean it that way, but it happens.
Have you experienced difficulties with organization, focus, or impulsivity in multiple settings, such as at home, in social situations, and at work, for most of your life?

Yes, it’s been that way as long as I can remember. Even back in grade school, my teachers would tell my mother I was smart but scattered. I’d talk out of turn, lose papers, and need reminders to finish my work. It wasn’t just one place or one time in my life.
Were you ever diagnosed with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder as a child?

I don’t think I was ever formally diagnosed as a child. If I was, nobody really told me that directly. I just remember teachers saying things to my mother, but I don’t know of any official diagnosis back then.
